text:
Arjun Patel: Heads up — noticed a regression on the long-seq path after the kernel-picker autotuner change. seq=2048 p99 up ~18% on the A10 pool, started ~2 hours after deploy.
Anya Lee: ugh, thanks. Which change specifically? the warp-specialization flags last night? :thinking:
Arjun Patel: autotuner started favoring the tiled=64 warp-specialized kernel for seq>1024. Previously the generic tiled=32 was winning. Profiling shows heavy register use + spill. nvprof snippet below.
perf-bot: perf-run/1830124679: job finished — baseline p99=420ms, current p99=495ms for seq=2048, batch=1.
Mica Rivera: can you paste kernel names + sm counters (regs/SMEM/occupancy)?
Arjun Patel: sure — quick excerpt from nvprof:
```
Kernel: kernel_tiled64_warp_spec
  Registers per thread: 64
  Shared mem per block: 11264 bytes
  Achieved occupancy: 0.375
  Local memory (spills): 192 stores

Kernel: kernel_tiled32_generic
  Registers per thread: 44
  Shared mem per block: 8192 bytes
  Achieved occupancy: 0.625
  Local memory (spills): 8 stores
```
Sato Nakamura: 64 regs/thread + ~11KB SMEM is rough on A10. That combo limits active warps -> latency goes up even if per-thread work is smaller. Warp-specialization probably inlines extra paths and raises reg pressure.
Taylor Gomez: also check whether KV-cache path increases live values per thread for long sequences — more live KV state + bigger tile size increases register usage.
Anya Lee: good call. For KV-heavy requests we saw higher active maps; autotuner doesn't yet account for KV footprint per request.
Mica Rivera: ran a micro-canary: forced kernel=generic for seq=2048, batch=1 -> p99 dropped to 438ms (still slightly above pre-change but much better than 495ms). So it looks like kernel pick is the main culprit.
Arjun Patel: proposed mitigation: add constraints to autotuner scoring — penalize kernels where reg_per_thread > 56 or shared_mem_per_block > 8192 on A10 targets, and prefer generic for batch<=2 on seq>=1536. Thoughts?
Sato Nakamura: sounds sensible. We should also add telemetry so we can see (kernel, regs, smem, occupancy) per invocation for a few days. That will validate heuristics.
Taylor Gomez: I'll open a PR Monday with:
- autotuner threshold changes
- a new perf test targeting seq=1024/1536/2048 on A10 with batch=1..4
- telemetry hooks + aggregate dashboard.
Command I used locally: `python infra/perf/run_local.py --model=gpt-small --seq=2048 --batch=1 --force-kernel=generic`
Anya Lee: also consider a middle tile (48?) — tile=48 might reduce reg pressure without killing compute efficiency. Worth an autotune sweep: `--tile=[32,48,64]` and measure regs/occupancy.
Mica Rivera: quick local sweep shows tile=48 -> regs ~52, smem ~9KB, occupancy ~0.52, p99 ~430ms. So 48 looks promising.
Arjun Patel: action items: Taylor -> PR + perf tests; Sato -> add runtime telemetry for chosen kernel + regs/smem/occupancy; Mica -> run broader tile sweep across A10/4090 and post results; Anya -> update release note that we temporarily roll back warp-specialization for long seqs on A10 if canary flags fail. I'll spin up a canary change to make autotuner avoid warp-specialized for seq>=1536 on A10 for now.
Taylor Gomez: assigning and will @mention when PR is ready.
perf-bot: canary-deploy/1830124748: rollout started to 5% of A10 pool.
Arjun Patel: thanks everyone. Let's re-evaluate after 24h of telemetry. :thumbsup:
